items.name: Crochet a coaster
items.about: The classic first crochet project: one small circle teaches the basic stitches.
howToSteps: Learn the slip knot and chain.
Make a magic ring and work single crochet into it.
Increase each round until it lies flat.
Fasten off and weave in the ends.

metadata.You'll need: Cotton yarn, a 4 mm hook, scissors
metadata.First win: A round coaster on your table

items.name: Crochet a small amigurumi
items.about: Small crocheted toys worked in spirals; a little ball or a whale is a great start.
howToSteps: Pick a beginner pattern: a ball, a whale or a cactus.
Work in a spiral and mark the first stitch.
Stuff it firmly as you close it.
Sew on the face last.

metadata.You'll need: Yarn, a 3.5 mm hook, stuffing, safety eyes or thread

items.name: Knit a scarf
items.about: Garter stitch all the way: the gentlest way to learn knitting and end with something wearable.
howToSteps: Cast on about 20 stitches.
Knit every row (garter stitch).
Count stitches every few rows.
Cast off and weave in the ends.

metadata.You'll need: Chunky yarn, two 8 mm needles

items.name: Make granny squares
items.about: Colourful squares that join into cushions, bags and blankets.
howToSteps: Learn one granny square pattern.
Make four in different colours.
Join them with slip stitches.
Decide what they'll become.

metadata.You'll need: Two or three yarn colours, a 4 mm hook
metadata.First win: Four squares joined into a bigger one

items.name: Embroider a hoop
items.about: Back stitch, satin stitch and French knots in a little design you can hang up.
howToSteps: Draw a simple design on the fabric.
Learn back stitch for outlines.
Fill shapes with satin stitch.
Trim the back and display it in the hoop.

metadata.You'll need: A hoop, cotton fabric, embroidery thread, a needle

items.name: Try punch needle
items.about: Loops punched through cloth make soft, rug-like pictures quickly.
howToSteps: Stretch the cloth tight in the hoop.
Draw a simple shape.
Punch in rows, keeping the needle low.
Fill the shape, then the background.

metadata.You'll need: A punch needle, monk's cloth, a hoop, yarn

items.name: Cross-stitch a bookmark
items.about: Counted crosses on a grid make neat little pictures and patterns.
howToSteps: Pick a small chart.
Start from the centre of the cloth.
Make every cross lean the same way.
Back it with felt.

metadata.You'll need: Aida cloth, thread, a tapestry needle, a chart

items.name: Set up a bullet journal
items.about: A notebook that is planner, diary and to-do list at once, made by you.
howToSteps: Make an index page.
Draw this month's calendar.
Add a simple habit or mood tracker.
Use it daily for a week, then adjust.

metadata.You'll need: A dotted notebook, a pen, a ruler

items.name: Keep a gratitude journal for 7 days
items.about: Three good things a day: a tiny habit that changes how a week feels.
howToSteps: Write three good things each night.
Be specific: who, what, when.
Read them back on day seven.
Keep going if you like it.

metadata.You'll need: Any notebook and pen
metadata.First win: Seven days of small good things

items.name: Make a travel journal of a trip
items.about: Tickets, notes, maps and drawings from a trip, glued into a book of memories.
howToSteps: Gather tickets, receipts and photos.
Give each day a page.
Write the best moment of each day.
Add a little drawing or map.

metadata.You'll need: A notebook, glue, tickets and photos from the trip

items.name: Start a scrapbook of your year
items.about: A page a month of photos, tickets and notes: the year in your hands.
howToSteps: Print a few photos each month.
Add one ticket or note per page.
Write the month's highlight.
Look back in December.

metadata.You'll need: A scrapbook, glue, photos, washi tape

items.name: Paint 5 watercolour postcards
items.about: Small paintings are less scary than big ones, and you can post them to friends.
howToSteps: Practise washes and gradients.
Paint a simple sky or landscape.
Let each layer dry before the next.
Send one to someone.

metadata.You'll need: Watercolour paper postcards, a small paint set, two brushes

items.name: Fill a 30-day sketchbook
items.about: One small drawing a day of whatever is in front of you: a cup, a shoe, a window.
howToSteps: Pick a small sketchbook.
Draw one thing a day.
Don't erase; keep going.
Compare day 1 with day 30.

metadata.You'll need: A small sketchbook, a pencil, a pen

items.name: Learn brush lettering
items.about: Thick downstrokes and thin upstrokes turn handwriting into lettering.
howToSteps: Practise the basic strokes.
Letter the alphabet slowly.
Join letters into words.
Letter a quote you like.

metadata.You'll need: Brush pens, practice sheets

items.name: Make dot mandala art
items.about: Rings of painted dots grow into a calm, symmetrical pattern.
howToSteps: Mark the centre.
Dot rings outward, evenly spaced.
Change colour each ring.
Seal it if it's on a stone.

metadata.You'll need: Acrylic paint, dotting tools or cotton buds, a stone or card

items.name: Paint a Madhubani motif
items.about: Bihar's folk art: bold outlines, double lines and every space filled with pattern.
howToSteps: Draw a fish or peacock outline.
Double every line.
Fill spaces with lines, dots and petals.
Colour in bright, flat colours.

metadata.You'll need: Paper, a black pen, colours

items.name: Paint a Warli scene
items.about: Maharashtra's Warli art: circles, triangles and lines that become people and villages.
howToSteps: Paint the background earthy brown.
Draw people from two triangles.
Add a dance circle or a tree.
Keep everything white and simple.

metadata.You'll need: Brown paper or card, white paint, a fine brush

items.name: Try block printing on fabric
items.about: Rajasthan's craft of stamping patterns onto cloth with carved wooden blocks.
howToSteps: Wash and iron the cloth.
Spread paint thinly on a tray.
Press the block firmly, then lift straight up.
Heat-set the paint once dry.

metadata.You'll need: A wooden block, fabric paint, a cotton cloth, a tray

items.name: Tie-dye a bandhani cloth
items.about: Gujarat and Rajasthan's tie-dye: tiny tied points make patterns of dots.
howToSteps: Pinch and tie small points of cloth.
Dye it following the dye's instructions.
Rinse until the water runs clear.
Untie the knots to reveal the dots.

metadata.You'll need: A white cotton cloth, thread, fabric dye, gloves
metadata.First win: A dotted bandhani dupatta or napkin

items.name: Draw a rangoli design
items.about: Patterns of coloured powder at the doorstep, made for festivals and everyday welcome.
howToSteps: Mark a grid of dots.
Join dots into a simple pattern.
Fill with colours from the centre out.
Take a photo before it's swept away.

metadata.You'll need: Rangoli colours or chalk, a clean floor space

items.name: Make air-dry clay earrings
items.about: Shape, dry, paint and seal: wearable art in a weekend.
howToSteps: Roll clay to an even thickness.
Cut shapes and poke the holes.
Dry for a day, then sand and paint.
Seal and attach the hooks.

metadata.You'll need: Air-dry clay, a cutter, earring hooks, paint, varnish

items.name: Fold 10 origami models
items.about: From a crane to a jumping frog, one square of paper becomes something new.
howToSteps: Learn the basic folds.
Start with a boat and a cup.
Fold a crane.
Make ten and display them.

metadata.You'll need: Square paper

items.name: Paint a clay diya
items.about: Plain clay lamps become festive with dots, lines and colour.
howToSteps: Wipe the diyas clean.
Paint a base colour.
Add dots and lines in contrasting colours.
Light them on a festival evening.

metadata.You'll need: Plain clay diyas, acrylic paint, a fine brush

items.name: Knot a macramé plant hanger
items.about: A few knots, repeated, turn cord into a hanger for your plants.
howToSteps: Cut eight long cords and loop them on the ring.
Learn the square knot.
Tie rows of knots, then gather at the base.
Hang it with a plant inside.

metadata.You'll need: Cotton cord, a wooden ring, a pot

items.name: Make a soy candle
items.about: Melt, pour and wait: a simple project with a cosy result.
howToSteps: Fix the wick to the jar's base.
Melt the wax gently in a double boiler.
Pour slowly and keep the wick centred.
Let it set for a day before lighting.

metadata.You'll need: Soy wax, a wick, a heatproof jar, a double boiler

items.name: Make a handmade card
items.about: A card made by hand means more than any bought one.
howToSteps: Fold the card neatly.
Cut and layer paper shapes.
Letter a short message.
Give it to someone.

metadata.You'll need: Card, paper scraps, glue, pens
metadata.First win: A card for someone you love
